root.label: FTC revises Amazon Prime refund settlement order

events.label: FTC revises Amazon Prime refund settlement order

slots.name: settlement amount
slots.sentence: Amazon is issuing refunds to eligible Amazon customers under a revised $2.5 billion settlement with the Federal Trade Commission to resolve allegations that the retailer deceptively enrolled customers in its Prime subscription service.

slots.name: maximum payment
slots.sentence: The FTC said last month that more consumers qualify for refunds from Amazon and also raised the maximum payment from $51 to $200.

slots.name: refunded amount
slots.sentence: As of September, Amazon had refunded more than $845 million to customers, with the company agreeing under the settlement to issue $1.5 billion in refunds and pay a $1 billion civil penalty.

slots.name: refund commitment
slots.sentence: the company agreeing under the settlement to issue $1.5 billion in refunds

slots.name: digital payment window
slots.sentence: You have 30 days to accept a digital payment to receive the funds, or 60 days to cash a check, if you opt for that method.

slots.name: check cashing window
slots.sentence: You have 30 days to accept a digital payment to receive the funds, or 60 days to cash a check, if you opt for that method.

slots.name: eligibility period
slots.sentence: The revised order requires Amazon to reimburse members who used up to 20 Prime benefits over a year and who signed up for Prime between June 23, 2019, and June 23, 2025.
